subject: Datadog + Grafana: technical sprint-zero & pairing request
messages:
From: Jane Li <jane.li@cloudsight.io>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: integrations@cloudsight.io
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 09:21:00 -0800
Subject: Re: initial sync — Datadog + Grafana workstreams

Hi Olga —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our engineering lead (cc'd) dug into the agent/OTLP options and we think a short 'sprint-zero' pairing session would help unblock both sides. Key asks from CloudSight:

- Validate OpenTelemetry exporter configuration for our proxy setup (we use an outbound proxy and mTLS).
- Confirm Datadog agent sampling + trace/span mapping with Redwood's inference runtime (KV cache heavy workloads).
- Quick pass at a Grafana dashboard template for latency percentiles and token-cost breakouts.

We can prepare a small shadow dataset and run in your sandbox. Proposed days: Nov 18 or 19 morning PST. Attaching a one-pager of our proposed scope.

Attachments: sprint-zero-agenda.pdf

Best,
Jane Li
Head of Integrations — CloudSight
jane.li@cloudsight.io
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Jane Li <jane.li@cloudsight.io>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: initial sync — Datadog + Grafana workstreams

Thanks Jane — this is perfect. Nov 18 AM PST works for our infra pairing slot. Marcus will lead the Datadog/OTLP mapping and Camila will own Grafana templating. A couple of leads from our side:

- We'll need a short access token for a sandbox Datadog account or a temporary API key (we can use a scoped org key).
- For the proxy+mTLS case, can you confirm whether your egress uses CONNECT tunneling or a side-proxy?

Camila: I asked for the Grafana templates we keep in the partner repo; I'll forward a baseline graph set (percentiles, p50/p95/p99, per-model token-cost). Marcus: let's pair on the OTLP trace schema — CloudSight's spans look like they include a vendor.trace_id.

I'll send a calendar invite for Nov 18 09:30 PST.

Olga Petrov
Senior Partnerships Engineer | Redwood Inference
olga_petrov@redwood.com

Attachment: dd-otlp-runbook-v1.md

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Jane Li <jane.li@cloudsight.io>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 08:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: initial sync — Datadog + Grafana workstreams

Quick note on the trace mapping work:

- Redwood runtime emits model_id, request_id, kv_cache_hit boolean, and token_count as attributes on span root.
- Datadog APM expects trace_id/parent_id and its sampling priority header; we'll supply a small shim to convert attributes to tags for Datadog if you can't change the exporter.
- If CloudSight can emit OTLP Resource attributes with service.name = "cloudsight-proxy" that will help routing in our dashboards.

Dylan, can you prepare a short sandbox playbook that contains the curl commands and an example OTLP payload? Keep the payload light (1-2 tokens) so CloudSight can validate connectivity without heavy cost.

—Marcus

From: Jane Li <jane.li@cloudsight.io>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 07:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: initial sync — Datadog + Grafana workstreams

Appreciate the clarity Marcus. For the proxy: we use CONNECT with mTLS; the egress path terminates at a sidecar that forwards OTLP gRPC. We'll provide a test cert and a small proxy config.

We're happy to use a scoped Datadog API key; I'll generate one and send to Olga via secure channel. Also attaching our Grafana templates (JSON) and a short example OTLP envelope.

Attachments: grafana-dash-templates.json

Jane

From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
To: Jane Li <jane.li@cloudsight.io>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:34:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Nov 18 pairing: agenda + sandbox URLs

Nice to meet the CloudSight team this morning — great session. Notes/action items from pairing:

- We validated OTLP over gRPC thru the CONNECT proxy using the test cert. Sample command below for reference:
  curl -X POST https://sandbox.redwood.com/otlp/v1/traces --data-binary @sample-otlp.bin --header "Content-Type: application/x-protobuf"

- Marcus checked trace->Datadog tag shim; changes are minimal and we'll ship a small auto-instrumentation helper.

Action items:
- CloudSight: provide final scoped Datadog API key (ETA: Nov 19 EOD).
- Redwood: publish the Grafana template to partner repo and a short how-to.md (ETA: Nov 20).
- Both: smoke-test span->trace linkage for request_id.

I've uploaded the session recording and the dashboard JSON to the shared Drive. Links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-dd-grafana

Camila Reyes
Developer Relations — Redwood Inference

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Jane Li <jane.li@cloudsight.io>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Nov 18 pairing: agenda + sandbox URLs (follow-up)

Small follow-up and close-the-loop:

- Received the scoped Datadog key via secure channel — thank you, Jane.
- Camila: please push grafana-dash-templates.json to the partner repo and open PR with how-to.md.
- Marcus/Dylan: can you confirm the helper shim will be backward-compatible with customers who already use our native exporter? We want to avoid changing any existing schema.

I'll also open a short joint RFC for the shim and tag mapping (internal owner: marcus_lin). If everyone is aligned we can mark the sprint-zero as complete and move this into an onboarding checklist for new ISV partners.

Next steps: PR by Nov 20 (Camila), RFC by Nov 23 (Marcus). If any blockers surface ping me directly.

Thanks all — nice collaboration.

Olga Petrov
Senior Partnerships Engineer | Redwood Inference
olga_petrov@redwood.com
